explanation:
I found no declaration in Mathlib, Batteries or Lean core that states this result.

The closest match is `NumberField.InfinitePlace.denseRange_algebraMap_pi`, which says `K` is dense in the product of `WithAbs v.1` over all infinite places. It is the weak approximation theorem. Getting the sign statement from it takes real work. You would have to choose targets of ±1 at each real place. You would also have to turn density in the product topology into inequalities on `embedding_of_isReal`. You would also have to show the resulting element is nonzero. That is far more than one or two lines.

I also searched Mathlib's `NumberField` files for sign, positivity and real-place lemmas, and for `totallyPositive`. Nothing relevant turned up.
